item.title: [LU-20264] Support ID mapped mounts
item.description:
Container systems (like podman, LXC, crun) and modern package managers (snap) want the capability to map container users to real users on the host system. This is typically done via ID mapped mounts [1]. For Lustre to support this, we must account for the mnt_idmap that VFS passes to the various filesystem operations. Additionally, we must adjust Lustre's server-side re-validation of capabilities to account for user namespace root.

 

[1] https://lwn.net/Articles/896255/

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment: I think the alternative is to mount Lustre directly inside the user namespace, which would work without any change to the Lustre code. But I guess that in case the containers access Lustre via a bind mount, the idea is to rely on the mnt_idmap that the VFS passes to the filesystem operations. The main difference from a usability perspective being that mounting Lustre directly inside a container requires a privileged container.

Your understanding is pretty much right. VFS handles most stuff. But the filesystem still needs to ensure it's using the real FS uid/gid found via the map_idmap that the VFS passes along. So it's not entirely invisible. But most of the changes are fairly mechanical. There are some tricky edge cases. VFS doesn't pass along a mnt_idmap for every operation. And Lustre server wants to do some re-validations of client requests. Some of these validations can be wrong under an ID mapped mount.

I don't get why the VFS alone could not handle that and the FS needs to be involved. I would have assume the mapping is done at high level, then converted to the real ID and this is the value that is checked and send on the wire. As the mappings are local per client, what we care about on server side, between clients, is the real FS uid/gid. No?

This implementation passes the testing in https://github.com/kdave/xfstests/tree/master/src/vfs. I've tested it manually with podman and snap - it seems to work fine. There's a few other test suites (from various tools) that we ought to run as well (https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow, https://github.com/containers/crun/tree/main, https://github.com/containers/podman/tree/main, and https://github.com/lxc/lxc). If those pass as well, then we should be in pretty good shape.

"Timothy Day <timday@thelustrecollective.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/65918
